Definition: to be extinguished; figuratively, to expire or be dried up
BiblicalUsage: To be quenched is to go out like a fire, and Job says the streams of the brooks vanish when the heat comes. The psalmist says his enemies compassed him like bees and are quenched as the fire of thorns, and Proverbs says the lamp of the wicked will be put out. Isaiah says the chariots and the army are quenched as tow.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the quenching of the wicked is God's promise that evil does not burn forever. The fire of thorns flares and dies, and the lamp of the wicked goes out, but the light of the righteous shines. I hold that God quenches what He did not kindle, and keeps burning what He did.
